note: Model exchanges are fictional and constructed for teaching purposes. They use different places and details from the tasks, so learners notice the chunks without being given the answers.

tasks.intro: Listen to (or read) a traveller at another station. Notice the phrases in bold.

model.speaker: Traveller
model.line: Excuse me, can you help me? My card doesn't work in the machine.

model.speaker: Staff
model.line: No problem. Where are you going?

model.speaker: Traveller
model.line: A return to Northgate, please. I'm coming back this afternoon.

model.speaker: Staff
model.line: That's six fifty. The train leaves from platform two.

model.speaker: Traveller
model.line: Can I pay by card here? And which platform does it leave from, sorry?

model.speaker: Staff
model.line: Yes, card is fine. Platform two. Go straight on, then turn left.

model.speaker: Traveller
model.line: Thanks very much for your help.

matching.situation: You want to go and come back on the same ticket.
You want to start talking to a member of staff.
You don't know where your train is.

tasks.intro: Listen to (or read) two friends at a different café. Notice the phrases in bold.

model.speaker: Staff
model.line: Hi, what can I get you?

model.speaker: Customer
model.line: Could I have a cheese sandwich, please? And for my friend, the fish soup.

model.speaker: Staff
model.line: Sorry, we've run out of the fish soup.

model.speaker: Customer
model.line: Oh. He's allergic to nuts. What's in the chicken salad? Does it have any nuts in it?

model.speaker: Staff
model.line: No nuts in that one.

model.speaker: Customer
model.line: Great, he'll have the chicken salad instead. To eat in, please. That's all, thanks.

matching.situation: Your first choice is sold out, so you choose something else.
You need to check the ingredients.

tasks.intro: Language practice only, not medical advice. Listen to (or read) a customer with a cough. Notice the phrases in bold.

model.speaker: Customer
model.line: Hello. I've got a cough. Can you recommend something for it?

model.speaker: Pharmacist
model.line: How long have you had it?

model.speaker: Customer
model.line: I've had it for three days. I'm not taking any other medicine.

model.speaker: Pharmacist
model.line: OK. Take this syrup twice a day.

model.speaker: Customer
model.line: How often should I take it? Twice a day? And should I see a doctor?

model.speaker: Pharmacist
model.line: Yes, twice a day. If it doesn't get better in a week, see a doctor.

matching.situation: You say when the problem started or how long it has lasted.
You need to check the instructions.
You want to know what to do if it doesn't get better.

tasks.intro: Listen to (or read) a guest at a different hostel. Notice the phrases in bold.

model.speaker: Guest
model.line: Hi. I have a booking under the name Chen.

model.speaker: Receptionist
model.line: Sorry, I can't see it. When did you book?

model.speaker: Guest
model.line: I booked it online last week. Here's my confirmation email.

model.speaker: Receptionist
model.line: Ah, it's for next Friday. And tonight we're full.

model.speaker: Guest
model.line: Is there another room available? Would it be possible to stay in a shared room? I don't mind sharing.

model.speaker: Receptionist
model.line: Yes, I have one bed in a shared room.

model.speaker: Guest
model.line: That works for me. Thanks.

matching.situation: You arrive and want to check in.
You show proof of your booking.
You politely ask for something unusual.
